quotes.text: With AI voice tools and deepfake video, a calm voice on a call or a familiar face in a video meeting no longer gives staff enough confidence on its own.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: It means the proof doesn't have to live in one central system that every other organization must call.

quotes.text: Verified ID checks whether the proof is genuine. It does not replace the organization's judgment about what proof it should require.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Think of the two checks as separate jobs. Credential verification checks the proof. Face check checks the person presenting the proof.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: MFA and passkeys prove control of a sign-in method, while Verified ID proves a signed real-world fact such as employment or completed training.
Every exchange has an issuer, a holder and a verifier, and verifiers can check signature, issuer, expiry and revocation without calling the issuer.
Face Check adds a live selfie comparison for high-risk moments like account recovery, onboarding or sensitive access packages.
hook: Strong sign-in security still does not prove who is behind the screen, especially at the help desk in times of deepfakes. This episode explains Microsoft Entra Verified ID, digital wallets and Face Check in plain English for identity and IT teams. You learn where verified credentials replace PDF and screenshot checks in onboarding, recovery and access requests.
